name: Gram (Chickpea)
reason: Pulse crop with high nitrogen fixing; thrives in dry Rabi soils.
guideSteps: Varieties: Select Pusa-362 or RVG-202. Treat seeds with Rhizobium culture.
Planting: Sow in October-November in rows spaced 30 cm apart.
Irrigation: Critical watering at branching and pod-filling. Do not overwater.
Harvesting: Reap when plants dry out, turn brown, and pods rattle when shaken.

name: Moong Dal
reason: Fast summer pulse crop that naturally fixes nitrogen, restoring soil health.
guideSteps: Variety selection: Choose SML 668 or IPM 02-3 for short duration summer growth.
Sowing: Broadcast or drill seeds in mid-March to April, spacing 25 cm x 10 cm.
Nutrition: Requires minimal nitrogen. Apply Phosphorus to encourage root nodules.
Harvest: Pick mature pods in 2-3 pickings as they ripen asynchronously.

name: Urad Dal
reason: Quick-maturing black gram pulse suitable for Rabi rice-fallow or Kharif season.
guideSteps: Variety: Select T-9 or Shekhar-2. Seed treatment with Trichoderma is suggested.
Spacing: Row spacing of 30 cm, plant spacing of 10 cm. Drill at 3-4 cm depth.
Watering: Typically rainfed. Supplement during extreme dry spells at flowering.
Harvest: Cut the crop when 80% of the pods turn black and dry.

name: Arhar (Pigeon Pea)
reason: Deep-rooted pulse crop that withstands drought and improves soil fertility.
guideSteps: Variety: Use UPAS-120 or Pusa-992. Treat seeds with rhizobial culture.
Sowing: Plant in June-July. Space widely (60 cm x 15 cm) due to branching habit.
Weeding: Perform two hand weedings within the first 45 days to control competitor weeds.
Harvest: Cut entire plants when pods turn brown; stack in bundles to dry before threshing.

name: Lentil (Masoor)
reason: Cold-hardy Rabi pulse that grows well in clay-loam and alluvial soils.
guideSteps: Variety: Choose Pusa Vaibhav or K-75. Treat with Rhizobium before sowing.
Sowing: SOW in late October or November with 30 cm row spacing.
Watering: Typically requires 1-2 light irrigations if winter rains fail.
Harvest: Cut close to the ground when plants turn golden-brown and dry.
